collection.text: Long ago, when they were wild and free, the wolves were savage but noble hunters, feared but respected. Now, under the spell of Boroth the Wolfheart, they are the loathsome creatures of the Dark Fey. Moving silently ahead of Boroth's armies, they presage battle and death and destruction.

These creatures of fierce grace inhabit only the wildest, most inaccessible mountains. So rare is the sight of one that throughout the Bloodmarch it is regarded as an omen of the greatest good fortune.

Vicious, powerful and bloodthirsty, the witless trolls have long been the willing servants of the Dark Fey. Blindly loyal to Boroth the Wolfheart, they guard the vast dungeons of the Dark Citadel of Maranor, standing ready to slay any who seeks passage.

Much ill has been spoken of dragons, but in truth they are wise and noble beasts. Their homeland is the Isle of Arungor, off the coast of the Last Northing where they live in friendship with the Dragonlords. Dragons will come to the aid of all good men in need and bear them swiftly through the skies to the place they seek.

Wrought long ago by the dwarven smiths of the Long Mountains and forged with dragonsfire Stormblade is a weapon of great power. The warrior who wields Stormblade is tireless in battle whilst his foes wilt with each blow.
In the Last Northing, Bloodbringer was the Sword of the Kings. He who wields Bloodbringer will command the loyalty of the Lords of the Arakai, leading them to battle and to glory.

Widowmaker was the Great Axe of Dwarfdom, in the age when the dwarves were one people. The war for its possession split Dwarfdom asunder and gave rise to the bitterness that still estranges the Long Dwarves from their kin, the Deeping Dwarves. A dwarf who wields Widowmaker in battle is said to be invincible.

Aranath, in the tongue of the Fey, is the Golden Sword. It was made many summers ago, before the Dark Fey became touched by evil. In the hands of any Fey Lord, it is a weapon of ferocious power. In the hands of any other, it brings ill-fate.

In the time of the first wars against the Dark Fey, Persuader was brought to the Bloodmarch by a Prince of the Gelm who had travelled south into Coromand seeking aid against Boroth and this axe was the magical gift he was given. He who wields Persuader is able to draw upon warriors from any stronghold not at war with his realm.

Wrought in the Iron Mountains by dwarven smiths who sought the favour of the King of the Delve, Skullcrusher is a weapon of great power in the hands of any Giant, such that in battle he will fight with the strength of two.

Forged with dragonsfire on the Isle of Arungor many long winters ago, Swiftwing makes its bearer as tireless as a dragon, needing no rest or shelter. Yet the wielder of Swiftwing should beware - if he is part of a fellowship, Swiftwing's magic will not work for its spirit is as free and lonely as the great beasts of Arungor.

Long have the Golden Fey dwelt on the Isle of Immiel in Glimormir, singing their songs and weaving their golden magic. Upon Immiel, their magic is so legendary against evil that Boroth dares not to assail the island even now but beyond their golden isle their powers fall away. Of all the peoples of the Bloodmarch, only the Golden Fey have no hostage held in the Dark Citadel.

The Giants are possessed of great strength, but they are slow-witted and often use their strength unwisely. Their mountainous realm, the Delve, lies in the south-east of the Bloodmarch, betwixt the Marish and the Great Ocean. The King's stepdaughter, Melinissa the Sweet, is held hostage in Maranor by the Dark Fey.

Touched by evil long, long ago and now trapped in darkness, the Dark Fey are consumed by an unquenchable thirst for power and dominion. Their King, Boroth the Wolfheart, will not rest until he has enslaved the entire Bloodmarch. Their realm is the Marish, in the southwest between the mountains of the Deeping and the Delve. There, in the dungeons of the Dark Citadel of Maranor, Mad Boroth keeps prisoners hostage from each of the realms of the Bloodmarch, to ensure their reluctant compliance.

Hardy and hospitable, the Long Dwarves dwell peaceably in their realm of the Long Mountains, which stretches half the length of the Bloodmarch, from the Mists of Oblivion in the far north to the borders of the Deeping in the south. Olthruda the Bountiful, the King's wife is held hostage in Maranor by the Dark Fey.

Possessed of much wisdom, but strange and enigmatic, the High Fey dwell in the Weirdwood in the west of the Bloodmarch, betwixt the Eldmark and the Gelm. Emedrel of the Fire, the High King's daughter, is held hostage in Maranor by the Dark Fey.

The Deeping Dwarves are a brave and resilient people. Their mountain kingdom, the Deeping, lies to the south of the Bloodmarch, between the Gelm in the west and the Marish in the east. Thalgrima the Betrothed, the King's bride to be, is held hostage in Maranor by the Dark Fey.

Friendly and good-hearted, the Gelmings dwell in the Gelm, in the southwest of the Bloodmarch,south of Weirdwood and the Deeping. Wythran the Weaver, dabbler in the webs of fate and the King's only son, is held hostage by the Dark Fey in Maranor.

The Dragonlords of Arungor have, over the years earned the trust and friendship of the dragons that dwell in the island's mountains. The Dragonlords are fearsome warriors and their island kingdom in the northeast of the Bloodmarch, off the coast of the Last Northing has seen no war for many a year. Sagrana Goldenwing, the King's sister, is held hostage by the Dark Fey in Maranor.

Proud and warlike, the Athelings dwell in the Lee in the north of the Bloodmarch, betwixt the Witherlands and the Long Mountains. Zenethor the Strong, King of the Lee, is held hostage by the Dark Fey in Maranor.

The Uskarg, a wild and warlike people, rule the Fallows, a kingdom in the east of the Bloodmarch bordered in the west by Dawnwood and the Marish, in the east by the Great Ocean. Djalina Snowheart, the King's daughter, is held hostage by the Dark Fey in Maranor.

A matriarchal people whose history stretches back into the mists of time, the Eldrin dwell in the Eldmark, south of the Witherlands, north of Weirdwood, in the west of the Bloodmarch. Princess Aremela, the Queen's daughter, is held hostage by the Dark Fey in Maranor.

An ancient, charmed race, pure of heart, strong of limb, long of life, the Dawn Fey dwell in Dawnwood in the heart of the Bloodmarch. To the east lies the Fallows, to the north the Last Northing, to the west the Long Mountains and to the south, the Marish. Aloroth the Fey, the King's brother, is held hostage in Maranor by the Dark Fey.

Proud and pure, strong in battle, simple in love, the Arakai dwell in the Last Northing, in the northeast of the Bloodmarch, between the Long Mountains and the Great Ocean. Further east lies the Isle of Arungor and to the south lies Dawnwood. Kiranda the Wild, the King's daughter, is held hostage in Maranor by the Dark Fey.

A once proud and powerful people whose days of glory have long since passed, the Kith dwell in the Witherlands in the northwest of the Bloodmarch, south of Midnight, west of the Lee. Mogrik the Witless, Prince of the Witherlands, is held hostage in Maranor by the Dark Fey.

Boroth the Wolfheart has been slain in battleinby*.

But, although Boroth's body lies broken and lifeless, this is not the end of the Wolfheart's evil. Even now, in the Dark Citadel, the wickedness that, centuries ago, seeped from the witching stone into the very foundations of Maranor has drawn his tortured spirit back into its bosom.
In the Dark Citadel, the Wolfheart has been reborn as a terrible wraith. Only the evil power of the Citadel sustains him now, like a great heart of black stone.
Although he can never venture forth again, Boroth has unleashed all his minions against the Blood March. To end his evil forever, Boroth must be slain again in the Dark Citadel of Maranor itself!
Boroth the Wolfheart has been slain in battleinby*.
With the Dark Citadel taken, there is naught to sustain his tortured spirit and the dark power that he fed on now tears Maranor asunder!

The Wolfheart has been vanquished, his evil has vanished and peace, at last, falls upon the Blood March. The trumpets sound, the flags of victory are hoisted. Midnight and the Free are safe once more!
Defending the Dark Citadel of Maranor,Boroth the Wolfheart has been slain a second timeby*.
With the Dark Citadel taken, there is naught to sustain his tortured spirit and the dark power that he fed on now tears Maranor asunder!

The Wolfheart has been vanquished, his evil has vanished and peace, at last, falls upon the Blood March. The trumpets sound, the flags of victory are hoisted. Midnight and the Free are safe once more!

collection.text: The Great Lake of Glimormir lies in the northwest of the Bloodmarch. On its western shore is the Eldmark, on the eastern shore the Lee and on the northwest shore are the Witherlands. In the midst of the lake lies the fair Isle of Immiel, home of the Golden Fey and seat of their King, Galahar the Calm. The realm of Glimormir is the one sanctuary in the Bloodmarch where the evil of the Dark Fey cannot penetrate, such is the power and purity of Galahar.

The Long Mountains begin in the far north of the Bloodmarch and sweep down to the southwest like a scimitar. In the north, they lie between the Lee to the west and the Last Northing to the east. Further south, they touch upon Dawnwood to the east, the Deeping to the south, Weirdwood to the west and the Eldmark to the north. The mighty River Imilvir cuts through the Long Mountains in the land of Scaradir before tumbling into Dawnwood. The Long Mountains are the realm of the Long Dwarves and there are seven lands within its borders, Erenim, Isilfrey, Thordroth, Farwain, Beomir, Scaradwin and Scaradir. In Beomir stands the Citadel of the King of the Long Mountains.

Weirdwood lies in the west of the Bloodmarch, south of the Eldmark, east of the Long Mountains and the Deeping, north of the Gelm. Through its midst flows the mighty River Imilvir. Weirdwood is the realm of the High Fey and there are nine lands within its borders, Elinvar, Merikith, Arelmar, the Shimmering Forest, Aradel, the Forgotten Forest, the Forest of Forever, the Whispering Forest and the Golden Forest. In the Shimmering Forest, near the banks of the River Imilvir stands the Citadel of the High King of Weirdwood.

To the east of the Bloodmarch lies the Great Ocean. In the north, it beats upon the shores of the Last Northing and separates the Isle of Arungor from the mainland. Further south, it crashes upon the shores of the Fallows, the Delve and the Marish. There are six seas within the Great Ocean, the Sea of Galorwain in the far north, the Sea of Fire betwixt Arungor and the Last Northing, the Weeping Sea east of Arungor, the Grey Sea east of the Fallows, the Sea of Skulls off the coast of the Delve and, east of the Marish, the Shining Sea which reaches south beyond the Bloodmarch to Coromand.

The Marish lies in the southeast of the Bloodmarch, west of the Delve, south of Dawnwood and the Fallows, east of the Deeping and the Gelm. Through the heart of the Marish flows the River Falthrang churning its way west from the mountains of the Deeping to the Bay of Ulmor and the Great Ocean. The Marish is the bleak and desolate realm of the Dark Fey and there are nine lands within its borders, Gliwain, Malgor, Dwardor, Barathor, the Plain of Death, Maranor, the Plain of Ravens and the Burning Plain. In Maranor, on an island in the Falthrang, stands the Dark Citadel of Boroth the Wolfheart, High King of the Dark Fey where hostages from all the realms of the Bloodmarch languish in the dungeons.

The Deeping lies in the south of the Bloodmarch, south of the Long Mountains, Weirdwood and Dawnwood, east of the Marish, west of the Gelm. Within its mighty ring of mountains lies Lake Tarefyr whose icy blue waters feed the swift-flowing River Caradwin. The Deeping is the realm of the Deeping Dwarves and there are seven lands within its borders, the Mountains of Thunder, the Mountains of Dawn, Ararak, Sharenor, Ildemar, Tharn, Zaragrorn and Tharn. In the Mountains of Thunder stands the Citadel of the King of the Deeping.

The Last Northing lies in the northeast of the Bloodmarch, west of Arungor and the Great Ocean, east of the Long Mountains, north of Dawnwood. Through its midst flows the mighty river Arelon, curling westwards from the Long Mountains to the Bay of Tharran and the Sea of Fire. The Last Northing is the realm of the Arakai and there are eleven lands within its borders, Sharmark, the Sapphire Mountains, Melibor, Rilleon, Elmir, Ravenfrey, Erefar, Galorbard, the Crimson Mountains, Orcar and Caramane. In Rilleon, on the northern bank of the Arelon, stands the Citadel of the King of the Last Northing.

The Land of Midnight lies to the northwest of the Bloodmarch, northwest of the Witherlands. Only a tiny portion of Midnight touches upon the Bloodmarch, but here, in Corelay, the mighty River Imilvir begins its southward journey to the Great Ocean. The Castle of Corelay, a short way north of the Imilvir, is bastion of Prince Morkin and the place where, if Luxor the Moonprince be rescued or perish, a mighty army of warriors from the four corners of Midnight will gather to march upon Boroth the Wolfheart and the Dark Fey.

The Delve lies in the southeast of the Bloodmarch. To the west is the Marish, to the east the Sea of Skulls and the Great Ocean.\x09The Delve is a mountainous land and it is the realm of the Giants. Within its borders are twelve lands, Grorn, Finrod, the Iron Mountains, Gagrun, Tark, Othrym, Skirol, the Big Mountains, the Isle of Storms, Thordrin, Athruk and Tark. In Skirol stands the Citadel of the Great King of the Delve.

The Gelm lies in the southwest of the Bloodmarch, west of the Marish and the Deeping, south of Weirdwood. The Gelm is the principality of the Gelmings and within its borders are five broad lands, Finfyr, Geremiel, Samarand, Gilgrath and Emergelm. In Samarand stands the Citadel of the Prince of the Gelm.

The Witherlands lie in the northwest of the Bloodmarch, east of the Lee, north of Glimormir and the Eldmark, southwest of Midnight. Through their midst flows the mighty River Imilvir before tumbling into the calm waters of Glimormir. The Witherlands are the realm of the Kith. Within the borders lie but three lands,\x09Eomir, Erifel and Sareon. In Eomir stands the Citadel of the Prince of the Witherlands.

The Fallows lies in the east of the Bloodmarch, north of the Marish, east of Dawnwood. Further east lies only the Great Ocean. The Fallows is the realm of the Uskarg and within its borders there are nine lands, the Isle of Alathor, Elinbrand, Arabar, Skordroth, Theodel, Cerrelm, Roreon, Athrudan and Erilmark. In Roreon stands the Citadel of the King of the Fallows.

The Lee lies in the north of the Bloodmarch, east of the Witherlands and the Eldmark, west of the Long Mountains, on the eastern shore of Glimormir. At the heart of the Lee lies Lake Elinmor from whence the River Eodral flows south into Lake Glimormir. The Lee is the realm of the Athelings and within its borders there are eight lands, Rilnor, Thumar, Sharvik, Imildral, Varorn, Melthor, Cerevere and Ceremelth. In Varorn stands the Citadel of the King of the Athelings.

Immiel, the fairest isle of all, lies in Glimormir in the northwest of the Bloodmarch. Here, all are kept safe from the ravages of the Dark Fey by Galahar the Calm, King of the Golden Fey and Lord of Immiel. His great Citadel stands atop the cliffs on the southern coast of the island.

The mighty river Imilvir winds its way through the length and breadth of the Bloodmarch, tumbling through mountains, forest and plains. The Imilvir is the Silver Road of the Blood March, where a ship may sail from the Witherlands to the Great Ocean.

The Eldmark lies in the west of the Bloodmarch, north of Weirdwood, south of the Witherlands, west of the Long Mountains and the Lee. On its eastern borders, the mighty River Imilvir flows south from Glimormir towards Weirdwood. The Eldmark is the realm of the Eldrin and within its borders there are but four lands, Arelban, Arunvere, Meranor and Erilan. In Arunvere stands the Citadel of the Queen of the Eldmark.

At the borders of the Bloodmarch, the good warrior will find the Mists of Oblivion and is well-advised to turn back before the mists thicken to impenetrable lest he vanish from the memory of his comrades forever, venturing instead to other less stricken lands.

Dawnwood lies at the very heart of the Bloodmarch, south of the Last Northing, east of the Long Mountains, north of the Deeping and the Marish, west of the Fallows. Through its green forest flows the mighty River Imilvir before plunging into the Bay of Eregoth and the Great Ocean. Dawnwood is the realm of the Dawn Fey and within its borders there are seven lands, Maralan, Romiel, the Forest of Songs, Carafel, Emerthen, Elorthard and Corithel. In Elorthard, south of the Imilvir, stands the Citadel of the King of Dawnwood.

The Isle of Arungor lies in the northwest of the Bloodmarch, off the coast of the Last Northing. To the north is the Sea of Galorwain, to the east the Weeping Sea and to the west the Sea of Fire. Arungor is the realm of the Dragonlords and within its borders there are nine lands, the Dragon Mountains, Angelf, Rildroth, Sarnoth, Erivik, Shrygal, Ashnar, Cormir and Aragor. In Ashnar stands the Citadel of the Dragon King of Arungor.

Within the realms of the Blood March all manner of beasts and artefacts abound. Read this chapter to discover what peril or boon lies in store when you chance upon such things.\x0D\x0DTouch the crystal ball to behold the catalogue of all beasts and objects.\x0DTouch the arrows to read other pages.\x0DTouch the book to turn to the index.

Behold the Blood March and all its realms marked upon this chart.\x0D\x0DTouch the points of the compass to move the eyeglass across the map.\x0DTouch the magnified eye to peer closer at a place or the naked eye to see a broader view.\x0DTouch the other symbols to reveal or hide signs of men and beasts and cities.\x0DTouch the signs on the map itself to read more about creatures and places there named.

Herein are revealed those men and women, fey and foul, dwarves and giants around whom the unfolding saga of the Blood March revolves.\x0D\x0DTouch the crystal ball to behold the catalogue of all heroes and villains.\x0DTouch the arrows to read of others.\x0DTouch the book to turn to the index.\x0D\x0DIf you know of this hero or villain...\x0DTouch the compass to see his location on the map.\x0DTouch the eye to take heed or no heed of his actions. If you do take heed, then his deeds will be reported to you in the Here and Now and written in the Chronicle of the Bloodmarch.\x0D\x0DIf he is in a fellowship, touch the group of figures to turn to his Fellowship page.\x0D\x0DIf he is one of the Alliance...\x0DTouch the walking figure to become this hero in the Here and Now.\x0DTouch his portrait to set the hero a new quest.\x0DTouch his shield to read of his warriors and to recruit more at friendly strongholds.

In this chapter you will find all manner of places described, so that the traveller may find his way though the lands of the Blood March with more ease.\x0D\x0DTouch the crystal ball to behold the catalogue of all the places herein.\x0DTouch the arrows to read other pages.\x0DTouch the book to turn to the index.

In this chapter, you play your part in the unfolding saga of the Blood March and the Black Citadel of Maranor.\x0D\x0DTouch the rearing horse to start the the action and then make your way through the Blood March toward your destiny.\x0DTouch the escape key to leave the action\x0Dand read of other things at leisure.\x0DTouch the book to turn to the index.\x0D\x0DCONTROLLING THE ACTION\x0D\x0DTouch these keys to control the action:\x0D\x0DESC Halt the action\x0DF1 Talk to someone\x0DF2 Attack someone\x0DF3 Attack a stronghold\x0DF4 Enter or leave a building\x0DF5 Mount or dismount a dragon\x0DF6 Board ship or go ashore\x0DF7 Pick up or drop a weapon\x0DF10 Rescue hostage\x0D\x0DMove close up to and look towards any person, creature or object you are interested in before touching the relevant key.\x0D\x0DControl your movements using the mouse:\x0D\x0DMOUSE LEFT Turn left\x0DMOUSE RIGHT Turn right\x0DMOUSE FORWARD Look down\x0DMOUSE BACK Look up\x0DCLICK LEFT Increase speed\x0DCLICK RIGHT Stop moving\x0D\x0DWhen riding a dragon:\x0D\x0DMOUSE FORWARD Dive\x0DMOUSE BACK Climb\x0D\x0DThe number keys change the point of view:\x0D\x0D1 Looking at you from ahead\x0D2 Looking at you from the right\x0D3 Looking at you from behind\x0D4 Looking at you from the left\x0D5 Following you\x0D6 Looking through your own eyes\x0D\x0DWATCHING THE ACTION\x0D\x0DWhen you are watching the action you see the hero or villain enact his given quest but you are helpless to intervene. All that you can do is to stop watching by touching this key:\x0D\x0DESC Halt the action\x0D

Herein the Book of the Blood March lists those fellowships of diverse race which, under your Power of Command, seek to defeat Boroth the Wolfheart and return the Blood March to peace and harmony.\x0D\x0DTouch the crystal ball to behold the catalogue of all the fellowships herein.\x0DTouch the arrows to read other pages.\x0DTouch the book to turn to the index.

In this chapter, events of note in the story of the Blood March are recounted so that none may forget the mighty struggle against the evil of Boroth and the Dark Fey.\x0D\x0DTouch upon the scroll to behold the calendar by months and touch upon a day to learn of what unfolded then.\x0DTouch the arrows to read other pages.\x0DTouch the book to turn to the index.

Here are pictured the heraldic devices of all those who have placed themselves under the Power of your Command to strive against the Black Citadel of Maranor.\x0DTouch upon any shield and straightaway, you will be granted the Power of Command to play that ally's part in the Here and Now.\x0DTouch the arrows to behold other pages.\x0DTouch the book to turn to the index.

Upon these pages, every subject to be found in this chapter is depicted.\x0D\x0DTouch upon any picture to learn more about the chosen subject.\x0DTouch the arrows to behold other pages of the catalogue.\x0DTouch the book to turn to the index.

Upon the pages of the calendar, each day in the Chronicle of the Blood March is pictured. Those days of little note are marked by no more than the shining of the sun, but days of feasting or mourning or battle are marked more distinctively.\x0DTouch upon a day to learn more of what unfolded then.\x0DTouch the arrows to behold other months.\x0DTouch the book to turn to the index.

collection.text: Prince Morkin and Araleth the White, Lord of Dreams, approached the Castle of Corelay. Morkin placed the Moonring upon his finger, lifted his fist to the sky and cried out, "For the Moonprince, for Midnight and the Free! Boroth the Wolfheart, you shall pay for this with your life!" and the air trembled.\x0D\x0DStill languishing in his cell, deep in the dungeons of Maranor, Luxor the Moonprince felt the slight tremble of hope and knew that his son had donned the Moonring at last and was marching forth against the Wolfheart. Likewise, Corleth and Arin Lord Blood, having at last found a way into the dungeons of the Dark Citadel, felt the same trembling hope touch their minds and knew, somehow, that they were no longer alone in their quest to rescue the Moonprince from Boroth's foul clutches.\x0D\x0DRorthron the Wise, having now reached the Citadel of Varorn in the Lee, also heard the faint whisper thrown forth by the Moonring. Suddenly, all grew clear to him as he bent his mind towards Luxor's plight. Anderlane of the Arakai, the unexpected gift, of course! Already, away in the Last Northing, there could be help at hand from Luxor's unsuspected kin. Rorthron looked into the east towards the Long Mountains and beyond them Rilleon and the Last Northing, then hurried on. The War of the Blood March was about to begin!\x0D\x0D*

Prince Morkin and Araleth the White, Lord of Dreams, hastened through the land of Midnight towards the Castle of Corelay and the Last Mountains.\x0D\x0DCorleth of Corelay and Arin Lord Blood\x09still wandered through the Dark Citadel of Maranor, seeking a way into the dungeons where the Moonprince was held.\x0D\x0DRorthron the Wise reached the River Eodral and crossed from Rilnor into Varorn in the Lee.\x0D\x0D*

Boroth's swift-winged raven reached the Citadel of Xajorkith in the land of Midnight and Boroth's ransom note was taken to Prince Morkin. How the tables had turned since the Icemark! Now it was he who must free his father!\x0D\x0DIf an army were to rescue Luxor, it could not be seen to come from Midnight. With a handful of warriors, Prince Morkin and Araleth the White, Lord of Dreams, set forth for the Castle of Corelay and thence to the Blood March.\x0D\x0DMorkin's son Corleth and Arin Lord Blood still wandered through the Dark Citadel of Maranor, seeking a way into the dungeons where the Moonprince was held.\x0D\x0DRorthron the Wise, on his way to the Crimson Mountains, journeyed through Rilnor in the Lee.\x0D\x0D*

Boroth's swift-winged raven flew over the Isle of Immiel and crossed Glimormir, reaching the shores of the Witherlands by nightfall.\x0D\x0DCorleth and Arin Lord Blood still wandered through the Dark Citadel of Maranor, seeking a way into the dungeons where the Moonprince was held.\x0D\x0DRorthron the Wise, on his way to the Crimson Mountains, journeyed through Thumar in the Lee, along the shore of Lake Elinmor.\x0D\x0D*

Boroth's swift-winged raven flew over Dawnwood and crossed the Long Mountains into Ceremelth in the Lee.\x0D\x0DCorleth and Arin Lord Blood still wandered through the Dark Citadel of Maranor, seeking a way into the dungeons where the Moonprince was held.\x0D\x0DRorthron the Wise, on his way to the Crimson Mountains, journeyed through Thumar in the Lee, along the western bank of the River Eodral.\x0D\x0D*

Boroth's swift-winged raven crossed the River Caradwin, out of Malgor in the Marish and into Corithel in Dawnwood.\x0D\x0DCorleth and Arin Lord Blood, seeking to rescue Luxor from Boroth the Wolfheart's clutches, found a secret way back into the Dark Citadel of Maranor\x0D\x0DRorthron the Wise, on his way to the Crimson Mountains, hastened through Thumar in the Lee, along the western bank of the River Eodral.\x0D\x0D*

Luxor the Moonprince, his grandson Corleth and Arin Lord Blood were flung into a cell in the Dark Citadel of Maranor. Boroth the Wolfheart, realising his prisoner's worth, decided to hold Luxor ransom but was persuaded by the Moonprince to release Arin and Corleth. Boroth then despatched a swift-winged raven to take his ransom note to Luxor's son, Prince Morkin in the faraway land of Midnight.\x0D\x0DMeanwhile, Rorthron the Wise, having learnt that Anderlane of the Arakai, Lord of the Crimson Mountains in the Last Northing, was the unsuspected son of Morkin and grandson of Luxor, had at last reached the borders of the Blood March and crossed south into the land of Thumar in the Lee.\x0D\x0D*

In the Bay of Ulmor, the raging storm drove Luxor's ship onto the rocky shore of the Marish, where it was torn asunder. The handful of survivors who scrambled ashore were beset by a band of Dark Fey warriors. The Moonprince already lay unconscious. In the battle, his old friend Lord Blood was slain defending him and his grandson Corleth and Lord Blood's son Arin were both struck down, alive but insensible.\x0D\x0DLuxor, Corleth and Arin were taken prisoner by the Dark Fey and carried off across the Plain of Death towards Boroth the Wolfheart's mighty stronghold, the Dark Citadel of Maranor.\x0D\x0D*

As Luxor's ship sped westwards through the Sea of Skulls, along the rocky coast of the Delve, the raging storm from the east finally caught them and drove the ship deeper into the west to the Bay of Ulmor, into the jaws of the Marish.\x0D\x0D*

Rounding the Isle of Storms, the wind changed and on the far horizon in the east, a mighty storm gathered. Fearing the worst, the captain of Luxor's ship changed course, sailing westwards along the southern coast of the Delve.\x0D\x0D*

Then Luxor's ship, bound for Coromand, set sail from the Isle of Immiel. The wind was fair and the ship sped swiftly south across Glimormir, reaching the shores of the Eldmark and the River Imilvir by nightfall.\x0D\x0D*

collection.text: The Citadel of Erifel is the foremost stronghold of the Kith and, for centuries, it has been the seat of the Princes of the Witherlands.
The Citadel of Varorn is the principal stronghold of the Athelings and, for centuries it has been the seat of the Kings of the Lee.
The Citadel of Arunvere is the jewel of the Eldrin and, since time immemorial, it has been the seat of the Queens of the Eldmark.
The Citadel of Beomir is the strongest redoubt of the Long Dwarves and, since it was first hewn out of rock, it has been the seat of the Kings of the Long Mountains.
The Citadel of Rilleon is the greatest fortress of the Arakai and, since the eagles flew north, it has been the seat of the Kings of the Last Northing.
The Citadel of Ashnar is the mightiest stronghold of the Dragonlords and, ever since the Time of Taming, it has been the seat of the Kings of Arungor.
The Shimmering Citadel is the greatest stronghold of the High Fey and, for a thousand years, it has been the seat of the Kings of Weirdwood.
The Citadel of Elorthord is the mightiest fortress of the Fey and, for hundreds of years, it has been the seat of the Kings of Dawnwood.
The Citadel of Roreon is the chief stronghold of the Uskarg and, for twelve reigns, it has been the seat of the Kings of the Fallows.
The Citadel of Samarand is the strongest fortress of the Gelmings and, for centuries, it has been the seat of the Princes of the Gelm.
The Citadel of Thunder is the mightiest redoubt of the Deeping Dwarves and, since the first king came into the mountains, it has been the seat of the Kings of the Deeping.
The Citadel of Skirol is the strongest bastion of the Giants and it has been the seat of the Kings of the Delve for many moons.

The Dark Citadel of Maranor is the mightiest bastion of the Dark Fey. It was the seat of the Fey Kings of the Marish even before the fall of the First Fey into evil. Now it is the foul lair of Boroth the Wolfheart, High King of the Marish, and in its dungeons he keeps prisoners hostage from all all the realms of the Bloodmarch.
The Citadel of Immiel is the fair fortress of the Golden Fey and has been the seat of the Kings of Glimormir for over a thousand years.
No citadel in the Great Ocean.
No citadel in the Mists of Oblivion.
